title: Arbitrary-Scale UAV Video Super-Resolution
description:
Against the backdrop of the booming low-altitude economy, drone aerial videos have become a core data source for fields such as land surveying and mapping, emergency rescue, and precision agriculture. However, constrained by payload power consumption and transmission bandwidth, raw videos often face bottlenecks like low resolution and blurred details, which restrict the effectiveness of downstream target recognition and scene analysis. As a key technology to break through hardware limitations and enhance data value, video super-resolution reconstruction serves as a crucial bridge connecting front-end data acquisition with back-end intelligent applications. To gather top-tier algorithm teams worldwide, explore the technological boundaries of spatiotemporal information mining, and tackle the challenges of detail recovery and texture enhancement in complex dynamic scenes, we are proud to host the Drone Video Super-Resolution Reconstruction Competition.

Through this competition, we aim to stimulate algorithmic innovation and improve system capabilities in high-fidelity temporal reconstruction and fine texture recovery under real-world aerial scenarios characterized by low resolution, high compression, and motion blur. This event will not only serve as a comprehensive assessment of technical strength at the intersection of computer vision and temporal signal processing but also provide forward-looking exploration for major applications such as all-weather intelligent surveillance, high-precision geographic information updating, and automated disaster assessment.
description_zh:
在低空经济蓬勃发展的大背景下，无人机航拍视频已成为国土测绘、应急救援、精准农业等领域的核心数据源。然而，受限于载荷功耗和传输带宽的制约，原始视频常面临分辨率低、细节模糊等瓶颈问题，这严重影响了下游目标识别和场景分析的有效性。视频超分辨率重建作为突破硬件限制、增强数据价值的关键技术，是连接前端数据采集与后端智能应用的重要桥梁。为汇聚全球顶尖算法团队，探索时空信息挖掘的技术边界，攻克复杂动态场景中的细节恢复和纹理增强难题，我们荣幸举办无人机视频超分辨率重建竞赛。

通过此次竞赛，我们旨在激发算法创新，提升真实无人机航拍场景中的高保真时间重建和精细纹理恢复能力——这些场景往往具有低分辨率、高压缩率和运动模糊的特点。该赛事不仅是对计算机视觉与时间信号处理交叉领域技术实力的全面考察，也为全天候智能监控、高精度地理信息更新和自动灾情评估等重大应用提供前瞻性探索。

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
### 🏆 1. Competition Overview

- **Competition Name:** CSIG Image and Graphics Technology Challenge - UAV Video Arbitrary Scale Super-Resolution Reconstruction Challenge
- **Organizer:** China Society of Image and Graphics (CSIG)
- **Co-organizers:** Sun Yat-sen University, Information Engineering University
- **Background:** Addressing the application requirements of UAV aerial video in national land surveying, emergency rescue, and other fields under the low-altitude economy, this challenge aims to solve the problems of low resolution and blurred details caused by hardware limitations. It seeks to enhance video super-resolution reconstruction capabilities through algorithmic innovation.

### 📅 2. Participation Requirements & Schedule

- **Eligibility:** Open to enterprises, institutions, faculty, students, and teams (maximum of 5 members per team) from across the country, as well as individuals.
- Key Dates:
  - **Registration Period:** June 3, 2026 – August 15, 026
  - **Testing:** August 15, 2026 – August 19, 026
  - **Competition Ends:** June 20, 2026 – August 20, 2026
- Platforms:
  - Competition Website: `[Codabench](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/edit/17147/)` 
  - Registration Link: [](https://v.wjx.cn/vm/OIAIWZk.aspx#)

### 📹 3. Competition Data & Task

 #### 	Dataset Composition:

- **Evaluation Set:** Includes 2 sets of UAV visible-light video datasets (covering scenarios like weak-texture roads and drastic viewpoint changes) and 1 set of UAV thermal-infrared video dataset (covering scenarios like edge blurring and low SNR).
- **Task Objective:** Input is low-resolution UAV video sequences. Output must support high-resolution reconstruction at arbitrary scales (4x, 6.7x, 9.8x, 12.9x).
- **Ground Truth:** High-resolution ground truth is provided for quantitative evaluation. Participants may select their own training data.

 #### 	Submission Requirements

Each participating team must submit the following materials:

- **Reconstruction results:** High-resolution reconstructed videos for all required test datasets, scale settings, sequences, and frames.
- **Code and documentation:**
  - Run scripts and source code required to reproduce the submitted results;
  - A technical report of no more than **3 pages** describing the method, experimental settings, and implementation details.

 #### 	Submission Methods

- **Direct Upload to the Competition Website:** Participants may directly upload the reconstruction results, code,  documentation, and technical report through the official competition  website.
- **Upload Through a File-Sharing Service:** Participants may upload the submission package to an approved  file-sharing service, such as Baidu Netdisk or Google Drive, and then  submit a text file containing the download link through the competition  website.



### 📊 4. Evaluation Criteria & Hardware Constraints

- Hardware Limits:
  - **CPU:** Xeon Platinum 8462Y+ / AMD Epyc 9534
  - **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / A100
  - **Memory:** 128GB DDR4
- Core Evaluation Metrics (Threshold Conditions):
  - **Pixel Accuracy:** PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio), SSIM (Structural Similarity Index).
  - **Perceptual Accuracy:** LPIPS (Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity), DISTS (Deep Image Structure and Texture Similarity).
  - **Temporal Accuracy:** tLP (Temporal Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity), tOF (Temporal Order Fidelity, estimated based on RAFT-Large optical flow).

| Scenario                               | Pixel Accuracy (PSNR/SSIM) | Perceptual Accuracy (LPIPS/DISTS) | Temporal Accuracy (tLP/tOF) |
| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| **General Requirement**                | PSNR≥28.0dB; SSIM≥0.750    | LPIPS≤0.250; DISTS≤0.180          | tLP≤12.00; tOF≤0.650        |
| **Visible Light Dataset**              | PSNR≥24.5dB; SSIM≥0.720    | LPIPS≤0.200; DISTS≤0.150          | tLP≤10.00; tOF≤0.600        |
| **Thermal Infrared Dataset**           | PSNR≥41.0dB; SSIM≥0.970    | LPIPS≤0.070; DISTS≤0.080          | tLP≤5.50; tOF≤7.50          |
| **Low-Light Night Scene (Additional)** | PSNR≥22.0dB; SSIM≥0.650    | LPIPS≤0.280; DISTS≤0.200          | tLP≤15.0; tOF≤0.800         |

### 📮 5. Contacts

- **Wang Hanyun** (Sun Yat-sen University): [wanghanyun@mail.sysu.edu.cn](mailto:wanghanyun@mail.sysu.edu.cn)
- **Dai Chenguang** (Information Engineering University): [cgdai2008@163.com](mailto:cgdai2008@163.com)
- **Li Wenke** (PhD Student, Sun Yat-sen University): [ieulwk@163.com](mailto:ieulwk@163.com)
- **Li Kangrui** (PhD Student, Information Engineering University): [kangrui.li21@outlook.com](mailto:kangrui.li21@outlook.com)

This competition closely aligns with the demands of the low-altitude economy, focusing on super-resolution reconstruction difficulties in complex UAV video scenarios. By setting strict metrics for pixel accuracy, perception, and temporal consistency, it aims to promote the practical application of computer vision technology in real-world aerial footage.

### 🏆 1. 竞赛概览

- **竞赛名称：** 中国图象图形学学会图像图形技术挑战赛 - 无人机视频任意尺度超分辨率重建挑战赛
- **主办单位：** 中国图象图形学学会（CSIG）
- **承办单位：** 中山大学、信息工程大学
- **背景：** 为适应低空经济发展背景下无人机航拍视频在国土测绘、应急救援等领域的应用需求，本竞赛旨在解决硬件限制导致的分辨率低、细节模糊等问题，通过算法创新提升视频超分辨率重建能力。

### 📅 2. 参赛要求与时间安排

- **参赛资格：** 面向全国企业、机构、教职员工、学生和团队（每个团队最多5名成员）以及个人开放。
- 关键时间点：
  - **报名时间：** 2026年6月3日 – 2026年8月15日
  - **提交时间：** 2026年6月20日 – 2026年8月20日
- 平台：
  - 竞赛网站：`[Codabench](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/edit/17147/)`
  - 报名链接：[](https://v.wjx.cn/vm/OIAIWZk.aspx#)

### 📹 3. 竞赛数据与任务

- 数据集组成：
  - **评估集：** 包括2套无人机可见光视频数据集（覆盖弱纹理道路、视角剧变等场景）和1套无人机热红外视频数据集（覆盖边界模糊、低信噪比等场景）。
  - **任务目标：** 输入为低分辨率无人机视频序列，输出需支持任意尺度的高分辨率重建（4倍、6.7倍、9.8倍、12.9倍）。
  - **标准真值：** 提供高分辨率标准真值用于定量评估。参赛者可自选训练数据。
- 提交要求：
  - 重建结果（高分辨率视频）
  - 代码和文档（运行脚本/源代码、技术报告≤3页）

### 📊 4. 评估标准与硬件约束

- 硬件限制：
  - **CPU：** Xeon Platinum 8462Y+ / AMD Epyc 9534
  - **GPU：** NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / A100
  - **内存：** 128GB DDR4
- 核心评估指标（阈值条件）：
  - **像素准确度：** PSNR（峰值信噪比）、SSIM（结构相似性指数）
  - **感知准确度：** LPIPS（学习感知图像块相似度）、DISTS（深度图像结构和纹理相似度）
  - **时间准确度：** tLP（时间学习感知图像块相似度）、tOF（时间序列保真度，基于RAFT-Large光流估计）

| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| **通用要求**                | PSNR≥28.0dB; SSIM≥0.750    | LPIPS≤0.250; DISTS≤0.180          | tLP≤12.00; tOF≤0.650        |
| **可见光数据集**              | PSNR≥24.5dB; SSIM≥0.720    | LPIPS≤0.200; DISTS≤0.150          | tLP≤10.00; tOF≤0.600        |
| **热红外数据集**           | PSNR≥41.0dB; SSIM≥0.970    | LPIPS≤0.070; DISTS≤0.080          | tLP≤5.50; tOF≤7.50          |
| **低光夜景场景（额外）** | PSNR≥22.0dB; SSIM≥0.650    | LPIPS≤0.280; DISTS≤0.200          | tLP≤15.0; tOF≤0.800         |

### 📮 5. 联系方式

- **王汉云**（中山大学）：[wanghanyun@mail.sysu.edu.cn](mailto:wanghanyun@mail.sysu.edu.cn)

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
## 1. Evaluation Objectives

This scoring scheme evaluates participating models across three complementary dimensions:

- **Pixel Accuracy:** Measures pixel-level fidelity between the reconstructed video and the corresponding reference video.
- **Perceptual Quality:** Measures visual similarity in deep feature space.
- **Temporal Consistency:** Measures inter-frame stability and penalizes flickering, texture drift, and temporal jitter.

The final score is calculated from PSNR, LPIPS, and tLP:

$$
\boxed{
TotalScore_i
=
0.60S_{i,PSNR}
+
0.25S_{i,LPIPS}
+
0.15S_{i,tLP}
}
$$

All metrics must be normalized to the interval $[0,1]$ before the weighted sum is calculated.

---

## 2. Test Dataset Description

### 2.1 Dataset Composition

The evaluation benchmark consists of **three test datasets**. Each test dataset contains:

- **4 scale settings**;
- **10 video sequences under each scale setting**;
- **100 consecutive frames in each sequence**.

Therefore, each test dataset contains:

$$
4\ \text{scales}
\times
10\ \text{sequences per scale}
\times
100\ \text{frames per sequence}
=
4{,}000\ \text{frames}
$$

The complete benchmark contains:

$$
3\ \text{datasets}
\times
4\ \text{scales}
\times
10\ \text{sequences per scale}
\times
100\ \text{frames per sequence}
=
12{,}000\ \text{frames}
$$

The dataset composition is summarized below:

| Item                                  | Quantity |
| :------------------------------------ | :------: |
| Number of test datasets               |    3     |
| Number of scale settings per dataset  |    4     |
| Number of sequences per scale setting |    10    |
| Number of frames per sequence         |   100    |
| Number of sequences per dataset       |    40    |
| Total number of sequences             |   120    |
| Number of frames per dataset          |  4,000   |
| Total number of frames                |  12,000  |

Unless otherwise specified in the dataset package, the scale settings, sequence names, directory structure, frame naming rules, and correspondence between input and reference frames are defined by the distributed files.

Participants must preserve the original dataset, scale, sequence, and frame organization when generating and submitting their results.

### 2.2 Dataset Download

The same dataset package, `test_datasets.zip`, is available through the following download channels.

**Baidu Netdisk**

- File name: `test_datasets.zip`
- Download link: <https://pan.baidu.com/s/1FhBYpV2ark_XuEx1Mmu4YA?pwd=8dg5>
- Extraction code: `8dg5`

**Google Drive**

- Download link: <https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Txyi40k_Q-skk3XKlOyVy2tKUaV6XcJ9/view?usp=sharing>

The packages obtained through the two download channels are intended to be identical. Participants should verify that the downloaded archive can be extracted successfully before running inference.

If an official file size or checksum is published separately, participants should use it to verify archive integrity. In the event of a discrepancy between the two mirrors, the version explicitly confirmed by the organizers shall prevail.

### 2.3 Dataset Usage Requirements

Participants must comply with the following requirements:

1. All three test datasets must be processed.
2. All four scale settings in each dataset must be processed.
3. All ten sequences under each scale setting must be processed.
4. All 100 frames of every sequence must be generated and submitted.
5. The output frame order must match the input frame order.
6. The original sequence names and frame identifiers must be preserved unless the submission specification states otherwise.
7. Output dimensions, file formats, color spaces, and bit depths must follow the official evaluation requirements.
8. Missing, duplicated, unreadable, incorrectly ordered, or incorrectly sized frames may cause the corresponding submission to be treated as invalid.

Test data may only be used in accordance with the competition rules. Any restrictions concerning external data, model pretraining, manual intervention, or test-time adaptation must be specified separately by the organizers and applied consistently to all participants.

---

## 3. Metrics and Weights

| Evaluation Dimension     | Role                  |  Metric   |    Direction     |  Weight  | Design Rationale                                             |
| :----------------------- | :-------------------- | :-------: | :--------------: | :------: | :----------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Pixel Accuracy**       | Core Metric           | **PSNR**  | Higher is better | **60%**  | Measures pixel-level reconstruction fidelity between the output and reference videos. Its dominant weight helps constrain color shifts, noise amplification, and overall distortion. |
| **Perceptual Quality**   | Perceptual Constraint | **LPIPS** | Lower is better  | **25%**  | Measures perceptual differences in deep feature space. It evaluates texture, local structure, and visual appearance, complementing the limitations of PSNR in reflecting subjective visual quality. |
| **Temporal Consistency** | Stability Constraint  |  **tLP**  | Lower is better  | **15%**  | Measures temporal perceptual inconsistency and penalizes flickering, texture drift, and temporal jitter across video frames. |
| **Total**                | -                     |     -     |        -         | **100%** | -                                                            |

This weighting strategy prioritizes pixel-level fidelity while using LPIPS and tLP as complementary constraints on perceptual quality and temporal stability.

---

## 4. Raw Metric Calculation Protocol

### 4.1 Unified Evaluation Conditions

To ensure fair and reproducible evaluation, all teams must be evaluated under identical conditions, including:

- The same test datasets and reference videos;
- The same scale settings;
- The same frame ranges and spatial regions;
- The same color space and pixel-value range;
- The same boundary-cropping policy;
- The same metric implementations, model versions, and parameters;
- The same frame-level, sequence-level, scale-level, and dataset-level aggregation methods;
- The same rules for handling invalid frames and abnormal samples.

The exact definitions and implementations of PSNR, LPIPS, and tLP must be fixed before the evaluation begins. In particular, the organizers should specify:

- Whether PSNR is calculated on RGB, Y, or another color space;
- Whether image borders are cropped before evaluation;
- The pixel-value range used in metric calculation;
- The network and version used for LPIPS;
- The exact definition and implementation of tLP;
- How the first frame or any undefined temporal pair is handled for tLP.

### 4.2 Hierarchical Metric Aggregation

To prevent a dataset, scale setting, or sequence from receiving unintended additional weight, the recommended aggregation procedure is hierarchical and balanced.

Let:

- $D=3$ denote the number of test datasets;
- $R=4$ denote the number of scale settings in each dataset;
- $K=10$ denote the number of sequences under each scale setting;
- $F=100$ denote the number of frames in each sequence;
- $m\in\{PSNR,LPIPS,tLP\}$ denote a metric.

For frame-based metrics such as PSNR and LPIPS, the sequence-level value is:

$$
V_{i,m}^{(d,r,k)}
=
\frac{1}{F}
\sum_{f=1}^{F}
v_{i,m}^{(d,r,k,f)}
$$

where $v_{i,m}^{(d,r,k,f)}$ is team $i$'s metric value on frame $f$ of sequence $k$, at scale $r$, in dataset $d$.

For a temporal metric defined over consecutive frame pairs, the sequence-level tLP value is normally:

$$
V_{i,tLP}^{(d,r,k)}
=
\frac{1}{F-1}
\sum_{f=2}^{F}
v_{i,tLP}^{(d,r,k,f-1,f)}
$$

unless the official tLP implementation defines a different temporal window or aggregation rule.

The scale-level value is:

$$
V_{i,m}^{(d,r)}
=
\frac{1}{K}
\sum_{k=1}^{K}
V_{i,m}^{(d,r,k)}
$$

The dataset-level value is:

$$
V_{i,m}^{(d)}
=
\frac{1}{R}
\sum_{r=1}^{R}
V_{i,m}^{(d,r)}
$$

The final raw metric value used for qualification, normalization, and ranking is:

$$
Value_{i,m}
=
\frac{1}{D}
\sum_{d=1}^{D}
V_{i,m}^{(d)}
$$

Because the benchmark currently contains the same number of scales, sequences, and frames in every dataset branch, this procedure gives equal weight to every dataset and scale setting.

If the organizers intend to use unequal dataset or scale weights, those weights must be fixed and published before submissions are evaluated. The corresponding general formula is:

$$
Value_{i,m}
=
\sum_{d=1}^{D}\alpha_d
\sum_{r=1}^{R}\beta_{d,r}
V_{i,m}^{(d,r)}
$$

subject to:

$$
\sum_{d=1}^{D}\alpha_d=1,
\qquad
\sum_{r=1}^{R}\beta_{d,r}=1
$$

---

## 5. Validity Checks and Qualification Thresholds

### 5.1 Submission Validity Checks

Invalid results must be excluded before qualification and normalization. A submission may be considered invalid if it includes, but is not limited to, any of the following:

- Missing, duplicated, or incorrectly ordered frames;
- Incorrect output dimensions or unreadable output files;
- Incorrect correspondence between output sequences and test samples;
- Incorrect dataset, scale, sequence, or frame directory structure;
- `NaN`, infinite values, or evaluation program failures;
- Outputs using an incorrect color space, frame rate, bit depth, resolution, or file format;
- Use of prohibited external data or other violations of the competition rules;
- Confirmed evaluation-system errors or otherwise invalid submissions.

A result must not be excluded solely because its metric value is unusually high or low.

Unless the competition rules explicitly define partial scoring, a submission missing any required dataset, scale, sequence, or frame is ineligible for the official ranking. This prevents teams from obtaining scores from only a favorable subset of the benchmark.

### 5.2 Recommended Qualification Thresholds

| Evaluation Dimension     | Metric |  Recommended Threshold  | Description                                                  |
| :----------------------- | :----: | :---------------------: | :----------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Pixel Accuracy**       |  PSNR  | $\ge 26.0\ \mathrm{dB}$ | Ensures a basic level of pixel-level reconstruction fidelity. |
| **Perceptual Quality**   | LPIPS  |       $\le 0.250$       | Limits severe perceptual distortion and texture artifacts.   |
| **Temporal Consistency** |  tLP   |       $\le 12.0$        | Limits visible flickering and temporal instability.          |

A team must satisfy all three conditions:

$$
PSNR_i\ge26.0\ \mathrm{dB}
$$

$$
LPIPS_i\le0.250
$$

$$
tLP_i\le12.0
$$

These values are **recommended thresholds**, not universal constants. Before formal adoption, they should be calibrated using the three test datasets, representative baseline models, the finalized metric implementations, and subjective human evaluation.

Once published, the thresholds must not be changed after the organizers have inspected participant results.

A team that fails any threshold is excluded from the official ranking. Its raw metric values may still be published with the status **“Did Not Meet the Qualification Thresholds.”**

If no team passes all three thresholds, the organizers must not silently change the thresholds after observing the results. The outcome should instead be reported, or a previously published fallback rule should be applied.

---

## 6. Determination of Normalization Bounds

Let the set of teams that pass both the validity checks and all qualification thresholds be:

$$
Q=\{i\mid i\text{ is eligible for the official ranking}\}
$$

For each metric:

$$
m\in\{PSNR,LPIPS,tLP\}
$$

the maximum and minimum values are:

$$
Max_m=\max_{i\in Q}(Value_{i,m})
$$

$$
Min_m=\min_{i\in Q}(Value_{i,m})
$$

Only teams eligible for the official ranking are used to determine the normalization bounds. Invalid submissions and teams that fail any qualification threshold are excluded.

For transparency and reproducibility, the final $Max_m$ and $Min_m$ values must be published with the competition results.

Because the bounds are determined from the participating teams, the normalized scores are suitable only for ranking teams within the same evaluation batch. They must not be directly compared across different competitions, test sets, or submission batches.

For cross-edition comparability, the organizers should instead publish fixed normalization bounds derived from representative baselines before the competition begins.

---

## 7. Metric Normalization

### 7.1 PSNR: Positive Metric

PSNR is a positive metric, meaning that a higher value is better:

$$
S_{i,PSNR}
=
\frac{Value_{i,PSNR}-Min_{PSNR}}
{Max_{PSNR}-Min_{PSNR}}
$$

After normalization:

- The team with the highest PSNR receives a score of $1$;
- The team with the lowest PSNR receives a score of $0$.

### 7.2 LPIPS and tLP: Negative Metrics

LPIPS and tLP are negative metrics, meaning that lower values are better. For:

$$
m\in\{LPIPS,tLP\}
$$

the normalized score is:

$$
S_{i,m}
=
\frac{Max_m-Value_{i,m}}
{Max_m-Min_m}
$$

Specifically:

$$
S_{i,LPIPS}
=
\frac{Max_{LPIPS}-Value_{i,LPIPS}}
{Max_{LPIPS}-Min_{LPIPS}}
$$

$$
S_{i,tLP}
=
\frac{Max_{tLP}-Value_{i,tLP}}
{Max_{tLP}-Min_{tLP}}
$$

After normalization:

- The team with the lowest LPIPS or tLP receives a score of $1$;
- The team with the highest LPIPS or tLP receives a score of $0$.

All normalized scores satisfy:

$$
S_{i,m}\in[0,1]
$$

### 7.3 Zero-Range Case

If all eligible teams obtain the same value for a metric:

$$
Max_m=Min_m
$$

the metric has no discriminative power, and the standard Min-Max formula would result in division by zero. All eligible teams are therefore assigned:

$$
S_{i,m}=1
$$

for that metric.

All teams consequently receive the same contribution from that metric, so it does not affect their relative ranking.

---

## 8. Final Score Calculation

The final score of team $i$ is:

$$
TotalScore_i
=
0.60S_{i,PSNR}
+
0.25S_{i,LPIPS}
+
0.15S_{i,tLP}
$$

When none of the metrics has a zero range, the expanded formula is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
TotalScore_i={}&
0.60
\left(
\frac{Value_{i,PSNR}-Min_{PSNR}}
{Max_{PSNR}-Min_{PSNR}}
\right)\\
&+
0.25
\left(
\frac{Max_{LPIPS}-Value_{i,LPIPS}}
{Max_{LPIPS}-Min_{LPIPS}}
\right)\\
&+
0.15
\left(
\frac{Max_{tLP}-Value_{i,tLP}}
{Max_{tLP}-Min_{tLP}}
\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

If $Max_m=Min_m$ for any metric, the special rule in Section 7.3 must be applied instead of directly using the expanded formula.

The final score satisfies:

$$
TotalScore_i\in[0,1]
$$

For publication, the displayed score is rounded to four decimal places:

$$
DisplayScore_i=\operatorname{round}(TotalScore_i,4)
$$

---

## 9. Ranking and Tie-Breaking Rules

1. Eligible teams are ranked in descending order using the full-precision, unrounded $TotalScore_i$.
2. Scores rounded to four decimal places are used for display only and must not determine the ranking.
3. If two or more teams have the same full-precision final score, the tie is resolved in the following order:
   - Higher raw PSNR ranks first;
   - If PSNR is equal, lower raw LPIPS ranks first;
   - If LPIPS is equal, lower raw tLP ranks first;
   - If all three raw metric values are equal, the teams are declared tied.
4. Teams that fail any qualification threshold are excluded from the official ranking.
5. Teams with invalid or incomplete submissions are marked separately and are not assigned an official rank.

---

## 10. Results to Be Published

For transparency and auditability, the official results should include:

- Submission validity status;
- Qualification status;
- Dataset-level PSNR, LPIPS, and tLP values;
- Final aggregated raw PSNR, LPIPS, and tLP values;
- Normalized PSNR, LPIPS, and tLP scores;
- The normalization bounds $Min_m$ and $Max_m$;
- The full-precision score retained by the evaluation system;
- The final score rounded to four decimal places;
- The official rank or ineligibility status.

Sequence-level and scale-level results should also be retained by the organizers for verification and dispute resolution.

---

## 11. Final Evaluation Procedure

The complete scoring and ranking procedure is as follows:

1. Download and verify the official `test_datasets.zip` package.
2. Process all three datasets, four scale settings per dataset, ten sequences per scale, and 100 frames per sequence.
3. Validate the structure and completeness of every submission.
4. Calculate PSNR, LPIPS, and tLP using the unified evaluation protocol.
5. Aggregate frame-level values into sequence-level, scale-level, dataset-level, and final raw metric values.
6. Apply the pre-published qualification thresholds to determine the eligible team set $Q$.
7. Calculate $Max_m$ and $Min_m$ for each metric using only teams in $Q$.
8. Normalize the three metrics according to their optimization directions.
9. Apply the zero-range rule whenever $Max_m=Min_m$.
10. Calculate the full-precision final score:

$$
\boxed{
TotalScore_i
=
0.60S_{i,PSNR}
+
0.25S_{i,LPIPS}
+
0.15S_{i,tLP}
}
$$

11. Rank eligible teams using full-precision scores and apply the tie-breaking rules where necessary.
12. Publish each team's displayed score, raw metrics, normalized metrics, normalization bounds, qualification status, and final ranking.

### 权重分配策略

该方案大幅提升感知度量权重，将LPIPS和DISTS确立为核心指标；采用像素度量作为基本保真度的约束；并使用时间度量保证视频质量的基线。

| 度量类别 | 角色 | 具体度量 | 权重（$W$） | 设计原理 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **感知质量** | 核心主导 | **LPIPS** | **30%** | 主要度量。深度学习超分辨率中与人类感知对齐度最高的度量。高权重鼓励模型生成丰富的高频纹理并避免过度平滑。 |
| | 细节辅助 | DISTS | 20% | 次要度量。结合结构和纹理失真，特别从无人机视角验证复杂地物（如树木、屋顶）的细节，防止伪影。 |
| **像素准度** | 基本约束 | PSNR | 15% | 主要度量。虽然权重降低，但仍保持物理基线作用，防止因追求感知质量而产生的严重色移或噪声放大。 |
| | 结构辅助 | SSIM | 10% | 次要度量。确保整体结构完整性，保证建筑轮廓清晰且无结构坍塌。 |
| **时间一致性** | 稳定性保证 | tLP | 15% | 主要度量。测量特征空间中的时间抖动。闪烁对视频任务是致命的；需要充分权重保证观看舒适度。 |
| | 运动验证 | tOF | 10% | 次要度量。在物理光流层面约束运动一致性，防止物体轨迹出现非物理跳跃。 |
| **总计** | - | - | **100%** | - |

### 详细计算公式

为公平比较不同量纲的度量，采用**最小-最大归一化**将所有度量映射到$[0, 1]$区间，然后进行加权求和。

#### 第1步：数据收集与极值确定
设参赛团队集合为$N$。对于每个度量$m$（如PSNR、LPIPS）：
- 识别所有团队中的最大值$Max_m$和最小值$Min_m$。
- *注：为防止极端异常值扭曲归一化，建议在确定Max/Min前排除前1%和后1%的极端值，或设定理论上下界（如将PSNR上限设为40dB）。*

#### 第2步：度量归一化
由于度量方向不同（越高越好与越低越好），必须分别处理：

**A. 正向度量（越高越好）：** PSNR、SSIM
$$ Score_{i,m} = \frac{Value_{i,m} - Min_m}{Max_m - Min_m} $$

**B. 负向度量（越低越好）：** LPIPS、DISTS、tLP、tOF
$$ Score_{i,m} = \frac{Max_m - Value_{i,m}}{Max_m - Min_m} $$

*其中$Score_{i,m}$表示团队$i$在度量$m$上的归一化分数（范围0到1）。*

#### 第3步：加权总分计算
$$ TotalScore_i = (0.30 \times S_{LPIPS}) + (0.20 \times S_{DISTS}) + (0.15 \times S_{PSNR}) + (0.10 \times S_{SSIM}) + (0.15 \times S_{tLP}) + (0.10 \times S_{tOF}) $$

最终分数应四舍五入至四位小数。

### 阈值条件审核（基于新策略）

为与新的加权系统对齐，建议同步更新参赛阈值。这确保高分团队不仅在感知上表现出色，还符合基本质量标准：

| 维度 | 度量 | 推荐阈值 | 说明 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **感知** | LPIPS | $\le 0.250$ | 核心阈值。超过此值表示纹理恢复能力不足。 |
| **感知** | DISTS | $\le 0.180$ | 辅助阈值。防止过度优化LPIPS导致的结构坍塌。 |
| **像素** | PSNR | $\ge 26.0 \text{ dB}$ | 适度放松（相比纯PSNR导向）。允许为感知质量牺牲少量SNR，但不可过度。 |
| **像素** | SSIM | $\ge 0.700$ | 确保基本结构相似度 |

### 📅 Competition Timeline

The competition is currently in the **Registration Phase**. According to the schedule outlined in the document, the key dates are as follows:

| Phase                 | Time Period                        | Status (as of Jun 16, 2026) |
| :-------------------- | :--------------------------------- | :-------------------------- |
| **Registration**      | June 3, 2026 - **August 15, 2026** | **Open**                    |
| **Testing**           | August 15, 2026 - August 19, 2026  | Upcoming                    |
| **Result Submission** | June 20, 2026 - August 20, 2026    | Upcoming                    |

### 🎯 Eligibility and Entry

- **Open To:** Teams and individuals from enterprises, institutions, universities, and colleges nationwide.
- **Team Size:** Each team must consist of **no more than five (5) members**.

### 💻 Technical Specifications

To ensure fairness and practical applicability, the competition enforces strict hardware and output constraints.

#### 1. Hardware Constraints

All solutions must be executable on hardware not exceeding the following specifications:

- **CPU:** Xeon Platinum 8462Y+ / AMD Epyc 9534
- **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / A100
- **Memory:** 128GB DDR4

#### 2. Submission Requirements

Participants must submit the following items:

- **Reconstruction Results:** High-resolution video outputs.
- **Code and Documentation:**
  - Executable scripts, programs, or source code.
  - A technical report (maximum 3 pages) including a method overview, innovations, runtime, and memory/GPU memory usage.

#### 3. Submission Methods

The submission materials may be provided through either of the following methods:

- **Direct Upload to the Competition Website:** Participants may directly upload the reconstruction results, code,  documentation, and technical report through the official competition  website.
- **Upload Through a File-Sharing Service:** Participants may upload the submission package to an approved  file-sharing service, such as Baidu Netdisk or Google Drive, and then  submit a text file containing the download link through the competition  website.

### 📊 Evaluation Criteria

The evaluation employs a multi-dimensional metric system to assess image quality, perception, and temporal consistency. The **threshold conditions** for qualifying submissions are detailed below.

#### Threshold Conditions for Qualification

Submissions must meet the following requirements across different scenarios to be considered valid.

| Scenario                            | Pixel Accuracy Requirements   | Perceptual Accuracy Requirements | Temporal Consistency Requirements |
| :---------------------------------- | :---------------------------- | :------------------------------- | :-------------------------------- |
| **General Requirements**            | • PSNR ≥ 28.0dB• SSIM ≥ 0.750 | • LPIPS ≤ 0.250• DISTS ≤ 0.180   | • tLP ≤ 12.00• tOF ≤ 0.650        |
| **Visible Light Dataset**           | • PSNR ≥ 24.5dB• SSIM ≥ 0.720 | • LPIPS ≤ 0.200• DISTS ≤ 0.150   | • tLP ≤ 10.00• tOF ≤ 0.600        |
| **Thermal Infrared Dataset**        | • PSNR ≥ 41.0dB• SSIM ≥ 0.970 | • LPIPS ≤ 0.070• DISTS ≤ 0.080   | • tLP ≤ 5.50• tOF ≤ 7.50          |
| **Low-Light Night Scene*(Optional)* | • PSNR ≥ 22.0dB• SSIM ≥ 0.650 | • LPIPS ≤ 0.280• DISTS ≤ 0.200   | • tLP ≤ 15.0• tOF ≤ 0.800         |

> **Note:** The Low-Light Night Scene is an **optional additional item** and is not part of the mandatory qualification threshold.

### 📥 Registration and Access

- **Registration Link:** [https://v.wjx.cn/vm/OIAIWZk.aspx#](https://v.wjx.cn/vm/OIAIWZk.aspx#)

- **Competition Website:** [https://www.codabench.org/competitions/edit/17147/](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/edit/17147/) (Website subject to change)

- **Data Download:** 
  The data are divided into reference data and test data.

  **Reference Data:**
  Baidu Netdisk: https://pan.baidu.com/s/16yE93GK0qu9rBbl0OsDdbA?pwd=v44u

  Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1lMhwIvSSgVgqVD9IA0W79thoqbrT9V9l?usp=drive_link

  **Test Data:**
  Baidu Netdisk: https://pan.baidu.com/s/1FhBYpV2ark_XuEx1Mmu4YA?pwd=8dg5

  Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Txyi40k_Q-skk3XKlOyVy2tKUaV6XcJ9/view?usp=sharing

| **成果提交** | 2026年6月20日 - 2026年8月20日 | 即将开始 |

### 🎯 参赛资格和报名
- **开放对象：** 来自全国企业、机构、大学和高等院校的队伍和个人。
- **队伍规模：** 每支队伍最多由**5名成员**组成。

### 💻 技术规格
为确保公平性和实用性，竞赛强制执行严格的硬件和输出限制。

#### 1. 硬件限制
所有解决方案必须可在不超过以下规格的硬件上执行：
- **CPU：** Xeon Platinum 8462Y+ / AMD Epyc 9534
- **GPU：** NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / A100
- **内存：** 128GB DDR4

#### 2. 提交要求
参赛者必须提交以下项目：
- **重建结果：** 高分辨率视频输出。
- **代码和文档：**
    - 可执行脚本、程序或源代码。
    - 技术报告（最多3页），包括方法概述、创新点、运行时间以及内存/GPU显存使用情况。

### 📊 评估标准
评估采用多维度指标体系来评估图像质量、感知质量和时间一致性。**通过资格的阈值条件**详见下表。

#### 通过资格的阈值条件
提交的成果必须满足以下要求，在不同场景中才能被视为有效。

| 场景 | 像素精度要求 | 感知精度要求 | 时间一致性要求 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **通用要求** | • PSNR ≥ 28.0dB• SSIM ≥ 0.750 | • LPIPS ≤ 0.250• DISTS ≤ 0.180 | • tLP ≤ 12.00• tOF ≤ 0.650 |
| **可见光数据集** | • PSNR ≥ 24.5dB• SSIM ≥ 0.720 | • LPIPS ≤ 0.200• DISTS ≤ 0.150 | • tLP ≤ 10.00• tOF ≤ 0.600 |
| **热红外数据集** | • PSNR ≥ 41.0dB• SSIM ≥ 0.970 | • LPIPS ≤ 0.070• DISTS ≤ 0.080 | • tLP ≤ 5.50• tOF ≤ 7.50 |
| **低光夜景场景**（可选） | • PSNR ≥ 22.0dB• SSIM ≥ 0.650 | • LPIPS ≤ 0.280• DISTS ≤ 0.200 | • tLP ≤ 15.0• tOF ≤ 0.800 |

> **注：** 低光夜景场景是**可选附加项目**，不属于强制性资格通过阈值。

### 📥 报名和获取
- **报名链接：** [https://v.wjx.cn/vm/OIAIWZk.aspx#](https://v.wjx.cn/vm/OIAIWZk.aspx#)
